routes.description: Establish that intelligible thought and inquiry depend on interconnected logical, epistemic, metaphysical, inductive, and ethical preconditions, and that the Orthodox Christian God supplies their coherent and necessary ground.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it connects unavoidable preconditions of discourse and experience to a specifically Orthodox metaphysical account, explains why non-theistic alternatives cannot supply the same unified justification, and defends the transcendental method used to establish that dependence.

motionBridge.description: Show that the preconditions of intelligibility cannot be coherently justified unless the Orthodox Christian God is presupposed.

centralBridges.description: Establish that paradigm-level presuppositions require transcendental assessment and that unavoidable circularity at this level does not reduce the case to an ordinary explanatory inference.
Show that attempts to deny fundamental logical norms still depend on logical regularities required for meaningful language, predication, and argument.
Connect scientific induction and natural regularity to a meta-level justification grounded in divine providence rather than merely assuming isolated regularities.
Explain how creation, divine archetypes, the logoi, and the essence-energies distinction ground shared intelligible content while preserving real distinctions.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish a non-Christian's practical use of reason from the worldview-level justification claimed to make that use coherent.
Relate the claimed logical and mathematical preconditions to the structures operative in actual human experience despite conceivable alternative formal systems.

routes.description: Show that the proposed transcendental reasoning does not establish that logic, induction, knowledge, ethics, or abstract content uniquely require the Orthodox Christian God, because the necessity inference and proposed grounding remain contestable.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it identifies a coherent non-Orthodox understanding of the relevant preconditions or shows that the affirmative method, necessity claims, induction account, and divine-conceptualist explanation do not establish the asserted exclusive dependence.

motionBridge.description: Show that the named preconditions can be understood without presupposing the Orthodox Christian God or that their alleged dependence has not been established.

centralBridges.description: Require a demonstrated connection between Orthodox belief and coherent thought rather than inferring necessity from the presence of worldview assumptions.
Show that challenges to classical logical laws can remain intelligible and that reductio does not establish universal non-contradiction against contradiction-tolerant positions.
Show that invoking providence does not nontrivially justify particular inductive expectations and may leave the underlying epistemic burden unchanged.
Develop non-theistic access to abstract objects and moral truths while testing whether divine thought explains shared abstract content without recreating the same distinction.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify whether the affirmative case is a transcendental proof, a paradigm-coherence comparison, or an explanatory inference, and identify the completion standard for that form.
Use alternative logics and geometries to test whether structures familiar in ordinary experience are genuinely necessary rather than contingently entrenched.

sections.title: Worldview Method and the Necessity Claim
sections.rationale: This issue governs the passage from unavoidable worldview assumptions to the motion-level conclusion that a specifically Orthodox presupposition is necessary, including the distinction between practical reasoning and ultimate justification.

sections.title: Induction, Natural Regularity, and Providence
sections.rationale: Induction is expressly named in the motion, and the central clash concerns whether providence supplies a meta-level justification for scientific regularity or merely relocates an assumption shared by competing accounts.

sections.title: Logic, Reductio, and Preconditions of Discourse
sections.rationale: This issue tests the operative transcendental method through non-contradiction, reductio, meaningful assertion, and alternative logics, determining whether denial of familiar logical principles undermines argument itself.

sections.title: Abstract Content and Orthodox Metaphysical Grounding
sections.rationale: The debate's claim of specifically Orthodox necessity depends materially on whether Platonist alternatives can explain abstract objects and whether the logoi and essence-energies account resolves shared conceptual content and participation.

sections.title: Actual Experience, Modality, and Alternative Systems
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether structures found in ordinary experience support logical or metaphysical necessity when non-classical systems remain conceivable, and how an experience-based formulation connects to the asserted modal conclusion.
